title: Why keep a positive balance, and when is a negative one fine?
description: A positive balance is generally better because a bank may charge a fee or interest on a negative one. A short negative balance can be worth it for a purchase that earns more soon, as in the business example from the book.
teaching_notes: One idea: a negative balance costs money, so it is worth it only for a short time and for a purchase that earns more soon. Watch for students who say a negative balance is always bad.

video_script.why: The child explains why a positive balance is better, and when a short negative balance is worthwhile.
video_script.substitution: Name the cost of a negative balance, then name a case where a short negative balance earns more than it costs.
video_script.payoff_line: A positive balance avoids fees and interest.

final_answer.value: A positive balance avoids fees and interest; a short negative balance can be worthwhile for a purchase that earns more soon.
final_answer.spoken: a positive balance avoids fees and interest, and a short negative balance can be worthwhile for a purchase that earns more soon

maths_rules: a positive balance means the money in the account is the account holder's own
a negative balance is money owed to the bank, and the bank may charge a fee or interest
a short negative balance can be worthwhile for a purchase that earns more soon
book example: the purchase left the balance −₹20, then a credit of ₹200 gave ₹180
